**TL;DR:** Lead with the answer in a sentence or two, so someone arriving from Bluesky or
Substack gets the point before any code.

## Question

State the question and why it's interesting. Link the paper the data come from and say what
this post adds: a different cut of the data, a new comparison, or a check of a claim. Cite with
`[@key]` from a `references.bib` file in the post's folder, like this [@chick2024].

## Data

- **Source:** GEO [GSE000000](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/) (placeholder)
- **Paper:** Author *et al.*, *Journal* (year), doi: …
- **Files used:** processed count matrix, as deposited
- **Accessed:** 2026-11-20

This example uses **simulated data** so it renders anywhere.

## Approach

Code is folded by default. Readers can expand any block, and everything needed to rerun the
analysis is on the page.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(1)
n_null <- 3800
n_de <- 200

res <- data.frame(
  gene   = paste0("gene", seq_len(n_null + n_de)),
  log2fc = c(rnorm(n_null, 0, 0.3),
             rnorm(n_de, sample(c(-2, 2), n_de, replace = TRUE), 0.6)),
  se     = runif(n_null + n_de, 0.25, 0.6)
)
res$pvalue <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(res$log2fc / res$se))
res$padj   <- p.adjust(res$pvalue, method = "BH")
res$status <- with(res, ifelse(padj < 0.05 & log2fc > 1, "Up",
                        ifelse(padj < 0.05 & log2fc < -1, "Down", "Not significant")))

table(res$status)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```

             89            3820              91 
```
:::
:::


## Results


::: {.cell .preview-image}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(res, aes(log2fc, -log10(pvalue), colour = status)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(Up = blog_palette[["accent"]],
               Down = blog_palette[["blue"]],
               `Not significant` = "grey70"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change", y = "-log10 p-value")
```

Refer to figures by label (@fig-volcano) and tell the reader what to look at. Tag the main
figure with `classes: preview-image` so it becomes the image on link previews.

## Caveats

Say what this analysis can't show: sample size, batch structure, whether the original
authors' processing was reused, and anything you'd check before trusting the result.
